System

Consensual player trading and escrow

A secure trade binds both players' acceptances to one immutable offer revision and commits both inventories/currencies together. Never implement trade as one player sending an item followed by a separate payment.

Scope and player interaction

A secure trade binds both players' acceptances to one immutable offer revision and commits both inventories/currencies together. Never implement trade as one player sending an item followed by a separate payment.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase19committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Requested → Editing → OfferChanged → AcceptedByOne → AcceptedByBoth → CommitPending → Completed → Canceled

WBP_Trade observes results from URPGTradeComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_TradePolicy_Default. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
TradeId UUID; ParticipantA/B CharacterIds; current OfferRevision
OfferItems: exact UUIDs/versioned stacks/quantities and currency integers
AcceptanceA/B: revision-specific; editing clears both acceptances
EscrowState: reserved/locked items or backend escrow locations under one authoritative policy
Eligibility: same safe zone/range, alive, not blocked, binding permits trade
CommandReceipt and ResultRevisionA/B: durable final outcome

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGTradeComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_TradeLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
RequestTrade(CommandId, TargetCharacterId) -> Invited|Blocked|OutOfRange
UpdateTradeOffer(CommandId, TradeId, ExpectedOfferRevision, Items, Currency) -> Updated|StaleOffer|BoundItem
AcceptTrade(CommandId, TradeId, OfferRevision) -> Accepted|OfferChanged
CommitTrade(TradeId, OfferRevision) -> Completed|NoSpace|OwnershipChanged; backend
CancelTrade(CommandId, TradeId) -> Canceled|AlreadyCommitted

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. A requests trade with B; backend validates both authenticated sessions, same-zone safe/range policy and blocks, then creates one trade record.
  2. Each offer update references exact items/currency. Reserve them under a declared backend escrow/lock policy so they cannot also be sold/crafted/equipped.
  3. Changing either offer increments revision and clears both acceptances; UI displays the revised item details/quantities prominently.
  4. Both accept the same revision. Backend locks both characters and escrow rows in sorted CharacterId order, rechecks binding/ownership/capacity/currency and active sessions.
  5. One transaction exchanges all items/currency, releases escrow, stores receipt and updates both revisions. A gear UUID moves unchanged.
  6. Disconnect/cancel before commit returns escrow atomically; after commit, cancellation returns AlreadyCommitted and both players reconcile the same final trade. Cross-zone transfer refuses while escrow is unresolved.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Create trade schema/contract and DA_TradePolicy_Default with safe-zone/range and item binding restrictions. Keep auction houses disabled.
  2. Build WBP_Trade with two clearly labeled offer panels, offer revision, currency, item tooltips, acceptance indicator and explicit confirm/cancel.
  3. Add URPGTradeComponent to authorized player/social route; inventory mutations consult escrow reservations.
  4. Reopen merchant/craft/equipment/bank to reject reserved items consistently; reopen zone transfer to drain/cancel unresolved trade before departure.
  5. Seed Sword_A and Ore_B, full-bag, blocked-pair, changed-offer and disconnect-after-commit fixtures.

Reopen Phase19 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_Rillmere / Trade_AB / Sword_A / Ore_B. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
B changes offer after A accepts -> both acceptances cleared; no old-amount commit.
Same item offered in two trades or sold concurrently -> reservation/ownership check rejects one.
Destination lacks capacity -> no partial exchange; escrow remains editable or cancels under policy.
Disconnect after committed trade -> both durable results remain; no return of already-traded items.
Bound item/negative currency/overflow -> rejected before commit.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Initial direct trade only, same safe zone, four items per side and bounded currency. Escrow timeout proposal 120 seconds. Expand only after contention/recovery tests, not before economy operations are stable.

Audit both participant IDs, offer revisions, acceptances, item UUID movement and receipt. Never obscure last-second offer changes; accessible confirmation is part of fraud prevention.
